ky_bronaugh_wall.blurb: Bronaugh Wall is a small wall in the Sore Heel Hollow part of the Pendergrass-Murray preserve, in the southern Red River Gorge. It holds 19 routes, nearly all of them bolted, plus a single trad line. Grades run from the high 5.9s into the 5.12s, with the bulk of the climbing at 5.11 and a good handful of 5.12s. Expect the Gorge's signature pocket pulling on sandstone, mixed with a few technical overhanging faces. The wall tends to hold shade through the afternoon, which suits warm days. Few routes means it works best as one stop in a longer day around the hollow.

ky_shady_grove.blurb: Shady Grove is a long, overhanging wall in Sore Heel Hollow, part of the Pendergrass-Murray preserve in the southern Red River Gorge. It has 19 routes, almost all sport with one trad line. The wall is shaded and shielded from sun and rain, which is where its name comes from. Climbing here is steep sandstone, and the grade spread is demanding: a few routes at 5.9 and 5.10, a solid middle at 5.11, a large cluster of 5.12s, and several 5.13s at the top end. It is a good pick for strong climbers who want cover on a hot or showery day.

ky_pirates_cove.blurb: In the Red River Gorge, Pirates' Cove is a small crag inside the Cliffview preserve, along the west edge of the Cowan Point peninsula. Of its 19 climbs, most are sport, with a few boulder problems and one trad line. The grades are friendlier than most of the Gorge: a spread of 5.6 through 5.12, with the largest share at 5.10, and easy V-grade problems under the roof for warming up. Terrain mixes slab, vertical wall, a sport chimney and dry roof climbing on sandstone. It is a newer, still-developing area, so check that holds are sound and wear a helmet.

ky_serenity_point.blurb: Serenity Point is a compact cliff in the Miller Fork preserve of the Red River Gorge, a short hike from the main lot. It has 19 routes, mostly sport with five trad lines. The climbing is concentrated in the 5.10s and 5.11s, with a few easier routes and a handful of 5.12s at the top. Two central 5.11s are the standouts. The crag catches morning sun and slips into shade by about 2 pm, so it works well as a warm-up stop in cold weather or an afternoon refuge when it is hot. Sandstone, with a pleasant variety of styles.

ky_corner_pocket.blurb: Corner Pocket is a southeast-facing sandstone crag in the Miller Fork preserve of the Red River Gorge. It has 19 routes, split fairly evenly between sport and trad. The faces are tall and mostly vertical, and the crag is known for a big cluster of good vertical 5.11s, with a scattering of easier lines, harder 5.12s, and hard projects in the amphitheater. Sun reaches the wall until mid-afternoon, so it is best on cool days. Approach from the left-hand end of the cliff. A good choice for climbers who like sustained vertical wall climbing.

ky_sanctuary_the.blurb: The Sanctuary is one of the hard-climbing crags in Muir Valley, in the Red River Gorge. It is mostly a steep sport crag with a few trad lines, 19 routes in all. The grades lean hard: a couple of moderates, a few 5.10s, then a heavy concentration of 5.12s and 5.13s, with one 5.14. The first wall is very steep and huecoed, while around the corner to the right the lines ease off and become more technical. The crag gets plenty of sun, though some routes stay dry in the rain. Best for strong sport climbers.

ky_cinema_alley.blurb: Cinema Alley is a string of smaller boulders along the path at the top of Sacred Ruins in the Foxtown bouldering area of Kentucky, running down toward the two huge boulders at the bottom. It holds 19 problems, all bouldering, and most are on the easy to moderate side: a few very easy problems, a big batch at V2, and a modest number of harder problems up to the V6 and V7 range. The first boulder you meet on the way down marks the start. Good for a relaxed circuit and for mixed-ability groups.
